title: Mask future tokens in causal attention
statement:
Step 6 · Attention

Autoregressive decoding must not see future tokens. Query at index i attends only to positions 0 through i, including itself. The first output must not change when future keys or values change.

Build it

Return a causal attention output for every query. All three sequences are nonempty and have equal length. Use the provided single-query attention helper.

Contract: Implement causal using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: queries = [[1, 0], [0, 1]], keys = [[1, 0], [0, 1]], values = [[10, 0], [0, 20]]
Expected: [[10.0, 0.0], [3.302384506733431, 13.395230986533138]]
Input: queries = [[1], [2], [3]], keys = [[1], [2], [100]], values = [[1], [2], [999]]
Expected: [[1.0], [1.8807970779778822], [999.0]]
Hint

Slice keys and values to the current position, rather than computing future scores.

Review your understanding

Why would unmasked attention make next-token training look better while breaking generation?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
